clue.text: In France, I may succeed politician in project to design aircraft

indicators.note: the word in tells us the politician and the French pronoun go inside the word for project

parts.note: to project is to stick out, or jut

indicators.note: to succeed is to come after, so the French pronoun follows the politician

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
je is French for I

explanation.surface: A French politician hopes to take over a scheme for designing a new aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may succeed' means comes after: the French pronoun follows the politician. A jump jet takes off vertically, like the Harrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump jet is a vertical take-off plane, a kind of flying machine.

clue.text: Raise a loan, initially, from a swindler

parts.note: to jack up is to raise, as a car with a jack

indicators.note: initially picks out the starting letter of the word loan

explanation.surface: Someone borrows money from a con man.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackal is used figuratively for a person who does dirty work or cheats others.

clue.text: Brummel's drunk — he's slurring his words

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Beau Brummell, the Regency dandy, has had too much and his speech is going.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummel's possessive 's gives no letter; 'drunk' signals the rearrangement of BRUMMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A mumbler speaks indistinctly, as a person slurring his words does.

clue.text: Doc's in the way of being cuddled by a bird — a dish!

indicators.note: being cuddled by means held within the arms of the bird's name

parts.note: the jay is a bird of the crow family
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
à la, French, means in the manner or way of

explanation.surface: A doctor is hugged by a bird, and a dish is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cuddled by' puts the doctor and the French phrase inside the bird; the second 'a' then closes the word. Jambalaya is from Louisiana.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Creole rice dish with meat or seafood.

clue.text: He may help retain the Ashes, say

definitions.text: He may help retain the Ashes, say

parts.words: He may help retain the Ashes, say
parts.note: the surface suggests a cricketer keeping the Ashes trophy, but the ashes here are trees an arborist keeps healthy

explanation.surface: An England player helps keep the Ashes cricket trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia Test cricket series; 'say' flags that ash is just one example of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist looks after trees such as ash, keeping them standing.

clue.text: Meander and talk on the way back? I might

definitions.text: Meander and talk on the way back? I might

parts.note: to meander is to wind, as a river does

indicators.note: on the way back means the word for talk is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: gab is idle talk

explanation.surface: Someone who rambles and chats all the way home describes himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns GAB into BAG. The whole clue also describes a windbag, who rambles and talks on.
explanation.definitionFit: A windbag is a person who talks at tedious length, wandering off the point.

clue.text: Fool's not beginning to show intelligence

indicators.note: not beginning tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for fool

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool fails to begin to show any brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit means mental sharpness or understanding.

clue.text: A majority of taxes must go up? Not at all

indicators.note: in a down clue go up means the letters read from bottom to top
a majority means most but not all, so the word for taxes loses its last letters

parts.note: revenue is money raised by taxes

explanation.surface: Will taxes mostly have to rise? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: REVENUE less its last two letters is REVEN; 'go up' reverses it to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Never is used emphatically to mean in no way whatever.

clue.text: Live broadcast, perhaps, should be quite fitting

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a broadcast is one example of something spoken

explanation.surface: A live broadcast ought to be quite suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags SPOKE (spoken out) as just one sense of broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke clothing is made to measure, so it fits the wearer exactly.

clue.text: A kind of service suitable to be put in soldier's inscription?

indicators.note: to be put in means placed inside the word for a soldier

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: A soldier's writing reads as a suitable church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is writing scrawled or scratched on walls.

clue.text: One who's joined whip-round for the food?

indicators.note: round means the word for whip goes around the word for joiner

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, the cat for short
a member is one who has joined a club or society

explanation.surface: A new club member contributes to a whip-round for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' reads as a collection of money, but it splits into a whip and the container signal 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese, eaten as food.

clue.text: A medium twisting about is a spectacle!

indicators.note: about means wrapped around the word is
twisting means the letters from A and the medium are turned around

parts.note: TV, television, is a medium of communication

explanation.surface: A psychic medium contorts about, which is quite a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' turns A plus the medium into VTA; 'medium' wants to be a psychic, but it is television.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing view, a sight worth seeing.

clue.text: Athletic side makes every ball a boundary

parts.note: all means every
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A football team's play turns every ball into a cricket boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: Alloa Athletic is a Scottish football club. 'Athletic' looks like an adjective, but it is part of the team name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa Athletic is a Scottish football team, so Alloa names the club.

clue.text: It's kind of daddy to introduce idle confection

parts.note: a sugar daddy is a rich older man lavishing gifts
to loaf is to idle

explanation.surface: Dad kindly introduces a lazy child to a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A sugar loaf is a cone of hard refined sugar, as sold in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugarloaf is a moulded cone of sugar, a sweet product of the confectioner.

clue.text: He's got lineages sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has put family trees into order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges GOT and LINEAGES; the whole clue also describes what such a researcher does.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogist traces family descent and pedigrees.

clue.text: By which one may see rep?

definitions.text: By which one may see rep?

parts.words: By which one may see rep?
parts.note: the letters p, r, e put in a new order spell the word rep, so a re-ordering of that prefix shows it

explanation.surface: A setup that lets one see a sales representative.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as PRE ARRANGEMENT: rearranging the letters PRE gives REP.
explanation.definitionFit: A prearrangement is something fixed in advance, here punned on rearranging a prefix.

clue.text: Going over end of the extract, to get information?

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word the

parts.note: a clip is an extract from a film
to sing is slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: Someone reads past the end of a passage in search of facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclipsing means passing in front of and blocking out, as the moon going over the sun.

clue.text: Trouble with basics when setting up a Cartesian co-ordinate

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the letters are mixed
in a down clue setting up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: as means when

explanation.surface: Problems with the basics arise when plotting graphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' rearranges BASICS to ABSCIS; 'setting up' reverses AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: The abscissa is the x-coordinate of a point on a graph.

clue.text: Gasbag usually avoided by high-fliers

parts.note: the surface suggests a bore shunned by ambitious achievers, but the gasbag is a tethered balloon that aircraft keep clear of

explanation.surface: Successful people steer clear of a bore.
explanation.walkthrough: Gasbag usually means a windbag, and high-fliers successful people; both are literal here, about wartime air defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered balloons were flown over cities in wartime to obstruct enemy aircraft.

clue.text: After revolution, see King die with common soldiers — the beast

indicators.note: after revolution means the whole string of pieces is turned around

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a die is a cube
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: After an uprising the king dies alongside his troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After revolution' turns the three pieces together, giving KCUBEOR backwards; 'see' is a link meaning look.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is a male roe deer, an animal.

clue.text: Have a go at me, always hiding the biscuits?

indicators.note: hiding means the letters sit concealed within the run of words before

explanation.surface: Someone dares another to take a swing, always keeping the biscuits hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is goATMEALways.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, and oatmeal biscuits are made from it.

clue.text: Scoundrel, for example, caught by distinguishing, mark? Not quite

indicators.note: caught by means held within the shortened word for mark
not quite means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a badge is a distinguishing mark

explanation.surface: A villain, for instance, is caught out by an identifying mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims the mark to BADG; 'caught by' then holds the example abbreviation inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a dishonest or disreputable person.

clue.text: Growing belief involves endless dispute

indicators.note: involves means the word for belief wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a credo is a creed or belief

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a scene is a noisy row or dispute

explanation.surface: A strengthening faith takes in a never-ending argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the dispute to SCEN; 'Growing' is a musical sense, a passage getting louder.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness, so it describes something swelling.

clue.text: She is caught by the Shakespear-ian tale-teller

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb, who wrote Tales from Shakespeare with his sister

explanation.surface: A woman is captured by a teller of Shakespeare's stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Shakespear-ian' is a line break in the printed page. Celia is Rosalind's cousin in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Celia is a female name, so it can stand for any woman, a her.

clue.text: Smug abstainer with a loaf

parts.note: pi is short for pious, smugly self-righteous
TT, teetotal, describes one who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A self-righteous teetotaller takes some bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread.

clue.text: Noisy row with the head?

indicators.note: noisy signals that the word for row is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to scull is to row with oars

explanation.surface: A loud quarrel with the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it means propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony framework of the head.

clue.text: The right gained a positional advantage …

annotationWithheld.why: The right gained a positional advantage … (9): no parse found giving PRIVILEGE from 'gained a positional advantage', which reads as PRIVILEGED; scan confirms the wording
annotationWithheld.clue: The right gained a positional advantage …

clue.text: Where you may make a note flat?

definitions.text: Where you may make a note
definitions.meaning: a notepad or writing ... is paper for jotting on
slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: Where can one jot something down in an apartment?
explanation.definitionFit: A writing pad is a block of paper for jotting, and pad is also slang for someone's lodgings or apartment.

clue.text: … with a week to pull back. Tricky!

indicators.note: back here means the word for pull is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: Given a week to retreat, things get difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAW reversed gives WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to deal with, difficult.

clue.text: Label a record in a foreign language

parts.note: a tag is a label
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone tags a disc in an overseas tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the main language of the Philippines.
